chapter: California, New York and Richard Himber
title: Almost joining Paul Whiteman's band
summary: Hirsch wanted Whiteman's drum chair but Whiteman would not take him from his friend Himber, and George Wettling got it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: He was the last of the fixers of us. So about that time, the one thing that I wanted more than anything in the world was to go with Whiteman's band. On drums. And the old man was just about ready but just before he hired George Wettling, he was talking to me. And then he found out that I was... Found out that I was going with the camera. And he...
Are you the same cat I let out? Do you want to go outside?
How did you get back in? Scremlins.
The obedient cat. The first one I've ever seen.

The old man Whiteman, Pops, he was such a good friend of my... Of... Of... Of him was, he wouldn't take me away from him. So that was the end of my... I got, I knew George Wettling very well. And... That was it. So I stayed with, I stayed with Dick.
